links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of chatbot responses to midlife health questions
links.effect: Even the most readable chatbot (Perplexity) had a grade level of 11.11 ± 1.93, so all chatbot responses were at or above roughly an 11th-grade reading level.
links.quote: Perplexity showed the highest score of 41.24 ± 10.57 in readability and lowest in grade level (11.11 ± 1.93), meaning its text is the easiest to read and requires a lower level of education.

unlisted_practices: Selecting among LLM chatbots by comparing expert-rated accuracy, relevancy, fluency, and coherence

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, readability, fluency, and coherence of six commercial LLM chatbots answering midlife health queries without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
